title: Stucco, red tile and a line about salsa
label: Brand gallery
lede: Two pages of the chain’s own website from the Internet Archive and three freely licensed photographs. The drawings are our own and do not reproduce the logo.

archive.caption: The home page of chi-chis.com, with online ordering, a to-go mascot and the slogan “Life always needs a little Salsa.”
archive.alt: A pale yellow home page with a cartoon to-go box, links marked by gold stars and a slogan about salsa
archive.credit: Cropped from an [Internet Archive capture](https://web.archive.org/web/19990422132200/http://www.chi-chis.com/) of April 22, 1999. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: The closing message that replaced the site.
archive.alt: An orange textured page with a single sentence ending in Adios
archive.credit: Cropped from an [Internet Archive capture](https://web.archive.org/web/20041010214646/http://www.chi-chis.com/main.htm) of October 10, 2004. Shown for commentary.

archive.caption: A Chi-Chi’s restaurant in Brussels, photographed in August 2011, seven years after the American chain closed.
archive.alt: A stone building with red neon Chi-Chi’s signs over two ground-floor arches
archive.credit: Photo: Sarah Stierch, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chi-Chi%27s_in_Brussels_-_Sarah_Stierch.jpg), CC BY 4.0.

archive.caption: A former Chi-Chi’s at the closed Parkway Center Mall, June 2013. The outline of the removed sign is still on the wall.
archive.alt: A stucco mall entrance with a red tile awning and the faint outline of removed letters
archive.credit: Photo: Nicholas Eckhart from Elyria, Ohio, United States of America, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chi-Chi%27s_at_Parkway_Center_Mall_(15061585908).jpg), CC BY 2.0.

archive.caption: A building identified by its photographer as a former Chi-Chi’s, trading as a buffet in November 2012. The colors are heavily processed in the original.
archive.alt: A bright yellow and red stucco restaurant with a tile roof and an Asian King Buffet sign
archive.credit: Photo: Corey Coyle, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Asian_King_Buffet_Former_Chi_Chi%27s_-_panoramio.jpg), CC BY 3.0.

drawings.title: The shelf.
drawings.caption: A jar of salsa and a bag of chips with blank labels: the grocery line that outlived the restaurants.[^28] Original illustration.

disclaimer: Colors were matched by eye to the photographs and are approximate. Chi-Chi’s is a trademark of its owner and is discussed here in historical and editorial context. The drawings are original illustrations and are not official assets.
